newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil in doldrums as winter demand static.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil in doldrums as winter demand static.

text.p: Forecasts of colder weather in parts of northern Europe failed to ignite a pre-Christmas heating oil buying spree on Thursday and kept NWE gas oil premiums notionally steady in quiet business, traders said.
"Even forecasts of snow in Germany failed to get people buying -- usually two days before Christmas there is a surge of business as people prepare for the cold," a trader said.
Steady efforts to work arbitrages to the United States produced no hard evidence of a successful trade.
Traders added that most refineries in the region appeared to have satisfied scheduled requirements for the rest of December.
Benchmark Jan futures ended $1.50 down at $217.75 following steady selling of the Jan-Feb spread.
Prompt heating oil cargoes were Jan IPE +$5/6. Cargoes for arrival in north Germany January 1-10 were offered at Jan IPE +$5 with offers around +$6.
Russians were +$2.50/3.50 but drew little buying interest. Low sulphur diesel cargoes were Jan IPE +$14.50/$15.50.
Prompt barges of refinery grade heating oil are around Jan -$1.50/-$0.50. Low sulphur diesel is assessed at Jan IPE +$10/11.
